A bigger digital product doesn’t automatically mean a better digital product. That’s something I wish more beginners understood. Before worrying about: 🤎 How many pages it should have ✨ Which Canva template to use 🤎 What colors look professional ✨ How much information you can fit inside Get clear on what the product is supposed to help someone do. Try this: This product helps [WHO] go from [PROBLEM] to [RESULT]. For example: Instead of: “I’m making a 40-page social media ebook.” Think: “I’m creating a beginner content planner that helps someone go from not knowing what to post to having their first week of content planned.” Now you have a filter. Does this page help them reach that result? Keep it. Does it only make the product look bigger? It probably doesn’t need to be there. That’s how I’m approaching the products I build too: Start with the problem. Define the useful outcome. Then build what supports it. Not the other way around. 🤎 Save this formula before you start creating your first digital product. #DigitalProducts #DigitalProductsForBeginners #DigitalMarketingForBeginners #FacelessDigitalMarketing #StayAtHomeMomBusiness
